Restore the R types of a dataset's columns

Source: R/types.R
store_restore_types.Rd

Data read from a dataset's files by other tools (arrow::read_parquet(), DuckDB, ...) carries the storage types: character instead of factor, double instead of difftime, integer or double instead of integer64, plain 64-bit integers instead of H3 cells. store_restore_types() gives back the R types recorded in the catalog's columns specification of dataset. No data file is read.

Usage

store_restore_types(x, st, dataset)

Arguments

x

A data frame, tibble or sf object.

st

A store connection made by store_connect().

dataset

Name of the dataset x comes from: the full name, or its last part when that is unique. Index tables (<dataset>__h3) are accepted.

Value

x with the columns restored, of the same class (data frame, tibble or sf).

Details

Each column of x whose name is in the specification is restored when its type is compatible:

  • factor and ordered factor from character or factor, with the recorded levels (also the unused ones). Values outside the levels become NA, with one warning per column giving the count.

  • difftime from double (taken in the recorded units) or difftime (converted to them).

  • integer64 from integer, integer64, or double when every value is whole and below 2^53 in absolute value; otherwise the column is left as it is, with a warning.

  • list from an Arrow list or a list: a bare list.

  • H3 cells (class rcs_h3): the h3, h3_main and h3_p<r> columns of geospatial datasets and index tables, and every column recorded as rcs_h3.

Other columns are left unchanged, silently. Columns are matched by name only: a computed column that reuses the name of a source column is restored as that column.

collect() of a query from store_open(), with either engine, already restores the types; this function is for data that reached R another way, such as a DuckDB query of your own on the views of store_duckdb().

See also

store_describe() for the recorded types (r_type), rcs_h3.

Examples

root <- file.path(tempdir(), "rcs-example-restore-types")
st <- store_connect(root, create = TRUE)
store_write(st, rcs_sim_table(100, seed = 1), "sales/daily",
  title = "Daily sales", description = "Simulated daily sales."
)
#> ℹ Writing "sales/daily": 100 rows in 1 file.
#> ✔ primary  C:/Users/EB2/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpotBngr/rcs-example-restore-types  1/1
#>   files sent  13.7 kB  0.3s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 1 file in 1 location. Catalogs updated.
path <- list.files(file.path(root, "sales/daily"),
  pattern = "\\.parquet$", full.names = TRUE
)
raw <- arrow::read_parquet(path[[1]])
class(raw$wait)
#> [1] "numeric"
restored <- store_restore_types(raw, st, "sales/daily")
class(restored$wait)
#> [1] "difftime"
unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
